Subject: Region pinning & temporary egress windows — APAC customer question

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security and privacy teams: Pacific Health needs assurances that customer data for our account will be pinned to APAC-region compute (data residency) except for rare, pre-authorised maintenance windows.

Specifically:
- Can Redwood commit to APAC-region pinning for our production workspace (GCP/asia-southeast) and provide an exception process for temporary egress to other regions (e.g., US) for infra maintenance or cache warm-ups?
- What is your process for documenting and approving those transient egress windows?
- We also need the current subprocessor roster and a DPA addendum that explicitly references region pinning and transient egress notice/approval.

Attached: SLA_requirements.pdf (high level asks from our compliance team). Legal is on copy.

Would appreciate a short call this week to align on timeline — Emma Li, Head of Security, Pacific Health.

Best,
Emma

Subject: Re: Region pinning & temporary egress windows — APAC customer question

Hi Emma,

Thanks — really helpful notes and great to meet you. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps:

Summary: Redwood supports per-customer region affinity (pinning) and we can commit Pacific Health's workspace to APAC compute. We also support controlled transient egress windows for maintenance or exceptional workflows, subject to an approval process and audit logging.

What we propose:
1) DPA addendum: We'll produce a draft DPA addendum that includes a region-pinning clause, a transient-egress policy (max allowed monthly window, notice period, and approval workflow), and requirements around notification and audit logs.
2) Subprocessor roster: We'll provide the current roster and highlight any subprocessors that may be located outside APAC and what controls apply.
3) Egress process: Our standard approach is a documented request + 72-hour notice for scheduled windows, emergency opt-in with 24-hour post-facto audit for critical patches. We can offer a tighter SLA for Pacific Health (e.g., 48-hour scheduled notice, emergency up-to-6-hour monthly window with justification).

Action items / timeline:
- I will share a draft DPA addendum by Thursday (attached: draft_dpa_addendum_v1.pdf).
- Kimberly, can you pull the current subprocessor export and convert to the template? (cc'd)
- Emma/legal: please confirm whether Pacific Health needs the 6-hour cap reduced or additional controls (e.g., HSM-only keys) before we circulate final language.

If that aligns, let's schedule a 30-minute working call on Wednesday or Thursday to walk the DPA language and approval flow.

Thanks — Jonas

Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 15:08:00 +08:00
Subject: APAC pin + temporary egress window — proposal and next steps

Emma / Pacific Health Legal,

Thanks for taking the call today. Per our discussion, here is the proposed commitment and next steps we agreed to:

Redwood proposal (summary):
- Region pinning: Pacific Health production workspace will be pinned to APAC-region compute (asia-southeast1). All persistent customer data and primary inference traffic will run in-region.
- Transient egress windows: Redwood will allow up to 6 hours of outbound processing to non-APAC regions per calendar month for Phoenix-style maintenance, cache warm-ups, or emergencies. Scheduled windows require 48-hour notice and a short justification. Emergency windows may be initiated with on-call approval and must be logged with a post-event report within 24 hours.
- Subprocessors: Attached is the subprocessor roster template (subprocessor_roster_template.csv). We will highlight any subprocessors that are US/EU-based and the compensating controls.
- DPA addendum: Draft shared (draft_dpa_addendum_v1.pdf). Legal noted two items: (1) explicit audit log retention period for egress events, (2) optional KMS routing language if Pacific Health requires HSM-backed key isolation.

Next steps and timeline:
- Redwood: Finalize DPA addendum incorporating Marissa's edits and send for signature via DocuSign by Mon 2026-12-07. (link: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/RDW-7432-dpa)
- Redwood Ops: Deliver populated subprocessor roster by 2026-12-06.
- Pacific Health: Review DPA addendum and confirm whether to require HSM-level key controls by 2026-12-10.

If Pacific Health wants a stricter egress cap (e.g., 2 hours/month) or a different approval flow, we can include that in the addendum — it will affect operational feasibility and pricing.

Attachments: draft_dpa_addendum_v1.pdf, subprocessor_roster_template.csv

Please reply to confirm and we will move the addendum to signature.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
